https://www.techtimes.com/articles/32165.text: Romania's Air Force on Sunday shot down a Russian Shahed-type drone over the Black Sea near the mouth of the Danube — the third consecutive day its F-16s have intercepted and destroyed an intruder in NATO airspace, and the clearest signal yet that Europe's eastern flank has moved from passive monitoring to active kinetic defense. Romanian President Nicușor Dan confirmed the 10:13 a.m. local time intercept over the Sulina–Chilia area, about 12 kilometers (7.5 miles) northeast of Sulina in Romanian territorial waters, and called the string of violations "inadmissible and intolerable." Romania's foreign ministry summoned Russia's ambassador, calling the breaches "repeated violations." Russia has offered no public comment on any of the three incidents. It has had 33 opportunities to do so: that is the number of times Russian drones have illegally entered Romanian airspace since Moscow launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022, according to Romania's Defense Ministry. Most of those were tracked and allowed to exit or crash. This past weekend was different — and the difference was not only political, but technological. Exchange rate as of July 27, 2026; conversions are approximate. Three Consecutive Days, Four Total Shootdowns Two Romanian F-16 fighter jets scrambled from the Fetești airbase, operating under NATO's command authority, and shot down Sunday's drone over the Black Sea. The first confirmed shootdown occurred Friday — Romania's first successful drone intercept inside its own airspace in the four years since the war began. A second intercept followed Saturday. In all, four Romanian drone shootdowns have occurred in coordination with NATO allies in recent weeks: three this weekend and one in May, when Romania-based F-16 pilots operating out of Lithuania shot down a drone over Estonian airspace. Romania's initial investigation confirmed Friday's drone as a Shahed-type one-way attack vehicle "used by the Russian Federation in its war of aggression against Ukraine," President Dan announced. Investigations into Saturday's and Sunday's drones were still ongoing. NATO SHAPE spokesperson Col. Martin O'Donnell corroborated that the Sunday aircraft "appears to be of Russian origin." The legal authority for these intercepts rests on enabling legislation that Romania's parliament passed and interim President Ilie Bolojan signed into law. The statute specifically authorizes Romania's military to "destroy, neutralize, or take control of" unmanned aircraft breaching Romanian airspace without permission — a provision that, for years, the government was reluctant to use despite repeated drone intrusions. Russia's Sub-Threshold Campaign: What 33 Violations Prove Thirty-three drone incursions do not happen by accident. Analysts tracking Russian airspace violations documented four NATO incursions in 2022, five in 2023, six in 2024, and then 18 in 2025 — a 200 percent single-year increase that a systematic review published by The Fulcrum in February 2026, corroborated against NATO press releases and Institute for the Study of War operational assessments, described as "a deliberate campaign rather than accidental spillover." That 200 percent jump was statistically and strategically significant — not a product of incidental navigation error, but a sustained probe of NATO's detection thresholds, response times, and political will to engage. The geography of the current incidents explains the mechanism. Russia has intensified drone strikes on Ukrainian port facilities along the Danube River delta — cities like Izmayil and Reni that sit in the narrow zone where Ukrainian infrastructure, Romanian territorial waters, and Black Sea shipping lanes converge. Shahed-type drones launched toward those targets must transit a corridor that clips Romanian airspace almost by design. Whether a given drone blows past the boundary through navigation error or deliberate route-selection, the strategic effect is the same: NATO airspace is tested repeatedly, at low cost, with plausible deniability. In late May, the consequences of that campaign became tangible. A Russian Geran-2 drone struck an apartment building in Galați, Romania, injuring two civilians — the first confirmed injuries from a Russian drone strike on NATO soil. A marine drone self-detonated near an oil terminal in the Black Sea port of Constanța in June. The pattern prompted Bucharest to accelerate both the legal framework enabling drone intercepts and the hardware to execute them. How Romania Is Actually Shooting Down the Drones: MEROPS and the F-16 Combination The headline actor in Friday's first shootdown was a Romanian F-16 — specifically, one of four jets (two Romanian F-16s and two Italian Eurofighter Typhoons deployed under NATO's air policing mission) that scrambled after Romanian radar detected the drone about 20 kilometers (12.4 miles) east of Sulina. One F-16 engaged the target with an air-to-air missile, downing the Shahed over unpopulated ground near the village of Padina, in Buzău County. Sunday's intercept, per Romanian defense reporting, involved F-16s from Fetești without Italian jets: a five-minute engagement from airspace entry to intercept. But the more strategically significant technology operating in Romania's airspace is MEROPS — an AI-guided interceptor drone system that Romania officially integrated into its national air defense architecture on June 24, 2026. Romania deployed it primarily along the Danube River corridor — exactly the zone that has experienced these repeated incidents. MEROPS was developed by Project Eagle, a U.S. defense technology startup founded and funded by former Google CEO Eric Schmidt after Russia's 2022 invasion. The company later rebranded as Perennial Autonomy and brought in former Pentagon innovation chief Will Roper alongside engineers from Apple, SpaceX, and Google. It recently received a $500 million ceiling contract from the U.S. Army's JIATF-401 counter-drone task force. The system's architecture is specifically engineered for the Shahed problem: A ground control station, mobile launch platform, and the AS3 Surveyor interceptor drone operate as a single integrated unit. The Surveyor is a roughly 3-foot (0.9-meter) fixed-wing drone that reaches speeds of up to 175 mph (282 km/h), faster than the Shahed-136's cruise speed of around 115 mph (185 km/h). Onboard AI combines thermal imaging, radio-frequency detection, and radar to autonomously locate and track targets, allowing MEROPS to function even in GPS- or radio-jammed environments where conventional air defense would degrade. Each Surveyor costs approximately $14,500 to $15,000 — versus a Patriot PAC-3 interceptor at $3.9 million to $5.3 million per shot, or even a single F-16 sortie that costs multiples of the drone it is shooting down. If an interception misses, the Surveyor deploys a parachute and can be recovered and reused. Crew requirement: four people — a commander, a pilot, and two technicians — deployable on the back of a pickup truck. The operational record behind those specifications is extensive. MEROPS entered classified service with Ukrainian forces in mid-2024. By the time Romania formally integrated the system, Perennial Autonomy's German production partner Twentyfour Industries reported the Surveyor had downed more than 4,000 Russian drones in Ukraine. U.S. Army Brig. Gen. Curtis King, commanding general of the 10th Army Air and Missile Defense Command, told reporters the system "conservatively" accounts for 40 percent of all Shahed-type drones destroyed by Ukrainian air defenses. That is not a secondary air defense contribution — it is the primary one. The Shahed-136: Why a 1970s-Propeller Drone Is NATO's Persistent Headache The weapon Romania is now shooting down is, in technical terms, a fairly simple machine. The Shahed-136 — which Russia manufactures domestically at its Alabuga Special Economic Zone in Tatarstan under the designation Geran-2 — is a delta-wing one-way attack drone measuring 3.5 meters (11.5 feet) long with a 2.5-meter (8.2-foot) wingspan and a total mass of about 200 kilograms (440 pounds), according to its specifications. Its rear-mounted Mado MD-550 piston engine drives a two-bladed pusher propeller to a maximum speed of about 115 mph (185 km/h) — barely faster than a car on a German autobahn. Its standard warhead weighs 50 kilograms (110 pounds); Russia has also fielded a 90-kilogram (200-pound) heavy warhead variant since 2024. That combination of slow speed, low altitude, and small radar cross-section makes the Shahed-136 genuinely difficult for traditional air defense radars designed to track fast-moving jets and missiles. Its guidance system pairs GNSS navigation with an inertial navigation backup, and Russia's upgraded Geran-2 versions have added GLONASS, 4G modems, Starlink terminals, and AI-based computer vision to improve accuracy and jam resistance. Debris analysis of downed drones has identified Western components throughout the airframe — Texas Instruments processors, Altera FPGAs, Analog Devices radio-frequency modules, and a Polish-built fuel pump — evidence of systematic sanction evasion through third-party supply chains. Russia was producing approximately 170 Geran-2 units per day at Alabuga as of early 2026. At a domestic production cost estimated between $20,000 and $50,000 per unit, the economics of mass attrition are straightforwardly favorable for the attacker: launch enough of them at Ukrainian port cities near the Romanian border, and some will breach NATO airspace without costing Russia anything it considers prohibitive. NATO Allies Rally Behind Bucharest Belgium's Foreign Minister Maxime Prévot called Sunday's incursion "a stark reminder of the ongoing threat Russia's war poses to European security" and confirmed that 300 Belgian troops are based in Romania as part of NATO's eastern flank force. Col. O'Donnell at NATO SHAPE framed the shootdown streak within the alliance's broader hardware push: "The shootdowns come as NATO, Romania, and other nations actively acquire ground-based interceptors to enhance allied and national air defense capabilities," he said, adding that "NATO is constantly on the watch and prepared to defend itself from any threat." Romania is not building this air defense layer alone. Poland deployed MEROPS alongside Romania along NATO's eastern flank. Lithuania purchased 48 MEROPS Surveyor interceptors from Perennial Autonomy on April 22, 2026, becoming the latest NATO member to field the system. In July, NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte announced the Drone Edge Initiative — a $40 billion commitment over five years for counter-drone capabilities, drone procurement, and operator training across the alliance. Romania itself signed a separate agreement with Israel's Rafael Advanced Defense Systems in June 2026 for a layered air defense package worth more than €2 billion (approximately $2.3 billion USD), adding a mobile short-to-medium-range system to fill the gap between MEROPS's close-range interception and Patriot's long-range coverage. Romanian Pilots and a Fast Calculation: What Five Minutes Tells You One detail in Sunday's intercept warrants attention. From the moment the Shahed breached Romanian airspace to the moment a Romanian F-16 shot it down, approximately five minutes elapsed. That is the operational signature of a force that is now authorized, equipped, and practiced — not a force still debating whether to act. For context: the September 2025 incursion that preceded the enabling legislation saw two Romanian F-16s track a Geran-2 for nearly an hour before it departed on its own. The contrast between that restraint and this weekend's five-minute intercepts measures exactly how much Bucharest's posture has shifted. MEROPS's April 2026 test at the Capu Midia Air Defense Training Range on Romania's Black Sea coast exposed one documented limitation: one interceptor failed to engage a maneuvering target during evaluation. The Shahed-136 does not typically maneuver aggressively — its slow delta-wing flight profile is optimized for range, not evasion — so the operational mismatch between that test failure and the drone's real-world profile is narrow. Whether MEROPS alone or the F-16s were responsible for this weekend's kills has not been confirmed by Romanian defense officials. What is confirmed: three drones are gone, three investigations are underway, Russia's ambassador has been summoned, and NATO's eastern flank has answered 33 violations with something it did not answer the first 30 with — a missile. Frequently Asked Questions How does the MEROPS counter-drone system work, and why is it better than a traditional missile? MEROPS uses an AI-guided interceptor drone — the AS3 Surveyor — to physically intercept and destroy incoming drones like the Shahed-136. Unlike a traditional surface-to-air missile (a Patriot PAC-3 costs $3.9 million to $5.3 million per shot), each Surveyor costs approximately $14,500 to $15,000. The Surveyor homes in on targets using thermal imaging, radio-frequency sensors, and radar guided by onboard AI, making it effective even when GPS or radio links are jammed. If an intercept misses, the Surveyor deploys a parachute, lands safely, and can be reused. This cost reversal — spending $15,000 to stop a $20,000–$50,000 drone rather than $5 million — is why the U.S. Army purchased 13,000 MEROPS interceptors in the early days of the 2026 Iran conflict at $15,000 each. Why does Romania keep getting Russian drones flying into its airspace, and has this been happening for a long time? Yes. Romanian defense authorities documented 33 Russian drone incursions into Romanian airspace between February 2022 and July 2026. Until Friday, Romania had never shot one down inside its own borders. The incursions happen because Russia conducts sustained drone attacks on Ukrainian infrastructure — especially port facilities along the Danube River delta — and the flight corridors to those targets brush Romanian territorial airspace. Security analysts documented an 18-incident year in 2025 alone — a 200 percent increase over 2024 — that multiple independent reviews characterized as a deliberate campaign to test NATO's response, not a series of navigation accidents. What exactly is the Shahed-136 drone Romania shot down, and how dangerous is it? The Shahed-136 — which Russia manufactures domestically as the Geran-2 — is an Iranian-designed one-way attack drone, 3.5 meters (11.5 feet) long, weighing about 200 kilograms (440 pounds), with a maximum speed of around 115 mph (185 km/h). It carries a 50-kilogram (110-pound) high-explosive warhead in its standard configuration, with a 90-kilogram (200-pound) variant fielded by Russia since 2024. Its combination of low speed, low altitude, and small radar cross-section makes it difficult for traditional radar systems. Russia uses them in mass salvos against Ukrainian energy infrastructure, port facilities, and population centers. One struck an apartment building in Galați, Romania in late May 2026, injuring two civilians. At an estimated domestic production cost of $20,000 to $50,000 per unit and a production rate of approximately 170 per day, Russia can sustain mass Shahed campaigns indefinitely at acceptable cost — which is why the drone-on-drone intercept model MEROPS represents is strategically critical for NATO's defense economics. What does Romania's decision to start shooting down drones actually mean for the rest of NATO? Romania's shift from passive monitoring to active kinetic engagement — shooting down three drones in three consecutive days — demonstrates that a NATO member can lawfully intercept intruding hostile drones, absorb Moscow's non-response, and face no immediate escalatory consequences. That precedent matters. It suggests the sub-threshold category Russia has used to probe NATO borders for four years now has a proportional military answer that does not trigger Article 5 or a direct Russia-NAT

https://telex.hu/belfold/2026/08/30/unge.text: Menü Kereső Unger Anna: Engem ne hívogasson se Magyar Péter, se senki más! – A kormányfő kommentben válaszolt Belföld frissítve Weiler Vilmos Állítsd be a Telexet megbízható forrásnak! Beállítom Körülbelül 150 fős létszáma lehet a Nemzeti Vagyonvisszaszerzési és Vagyonvédelmi Hivatalnak, aminek nagyjából a fele nyomozati ügyekkel fog foglalkozni – mondta Unger Anna, a hivatal frissen kinevezett elnöke az RTL Házon Kívül című műsorának adott interjújában . Ungernek kedden lesz az első munkanapja, azt ugyanakkor, hogy aznap hol kell majd megjelennie, még nem tudta megmondani, azt csak holnap fogja megtudni. A májusi kormányalakítás után a Tisza Párt egyik első lépése volt a Nemzeti Vagyonvisszaszerzési és Vagyonvédelmi Hivatal felállítását lehetővé tevő törvény elfogadása. A törvény értelmében a szervezet elnöki és négy alelnöki pozíciójára pályázatot hirdettek, végül azonban csak az elnöki és a nyomozati elnökhelyettesi pozíciót töltötték be: az elsőt Unger Anna politológus, a másodikat Tasnády Katalin ügyész kapta meg. Őket pénteken nevezték ki a pozíciójukra, és most azzal a meglehetősen nehéz feladattal indulnak, hogy a nulláról kell felépíteniük a frissen létrehozott szervezetet. „Kedden el kell kezdeni felépíteni ezt a hivatalt” – mondta erről Unger, hozzátéve, hogy ennek rengeteg apró, kívülről alig látszó része van, amelyek nagy munkát fognak igénybe venni. A legfontosabb feladatuk most az, hogy munkatársakkal töltsék fel a hivatalt. Unger elmondása szerint a személyzeti állományról részben ő dönthet majd, a különböző részlegeket vezető elnökhelyetteseknek azonban nagy autonómiájuk lesz abban, hogy a saját részlegeiken belül kikkel szeretnének majd együtt dolgozni. Unger szerint emiatt most a legsürgősebb feladat, hogy újra kiírják azokat a pályázatokat, amelyekkel azt a három elnökhelyettesi pozíciót fel akarják tölteni, amelyet első körben nem sikerült. Erre értelemszerűen azért van szükség, mert a saját részlegeik felállításában nekik is nagy feladatuk lesz. Az interjúban az RTL rákérdezett arra, hogy kiket terveznek felvenni, amire Unger azt mondta, hogy „vannak a fejemben nevek”, olyanok is, akikkel korábban együtt dolgozott, és olyanok is, akikről tudja, hogy máshol nagyon jó munkát végeztek. Konkrét személyeket ugyanakkor nem nevezett meg, de azt elárulta, hogy a többségük a terveik szerint az ügyészségtől, a rendőrségtől és a NAV-tól érkezik majd. Unger elmondása szerint az ő feladata lesz az, hogy „elkérje” ezektől a szervezetektől az NVVH-s munkára kiszemelt dolgozókat. Arra a kérdésre, hogy mi történik, ha a szervezetek „nem adják oda” a munkatársaikat, Unger azt mondta, hogy megpróbálnak majd olyan ösztönzőket kitalálni, amelyekkel a szakemberek motiváltak lesznek a váltásra. Mivel a tervek szerint a hivatal legnagyobb részlege a nyomozati osztály lesz, az annak élére kinevezett Tasnády Katalinnak Unger szerint „a lehető leghamarabb” le kell majd adnia a névsort, hogy kikkel szeretne együtt dolgozni, hogy őket aztán minél hamarabb fel tudják venni. Unger szerint, ha ezzel jól haladnak, akkor már szeptember második felében el tudják kezdeni a nyomozati munkát. Az RTL rákérdezett, hogy vannak-e már konkrét ügyek, amiken az NVVH dolgozni szeretne, amire Unger azt mondta, hogy vannak, de a nyomozás sikeressége érdekében nem szeretnének ezekről semmit elárulni. Annyit azért elmondott, hogy a legegyszerűbb dolguk azokkal az elmúlt egy évben kötött szerződésekkel van, amelyeket túlárazottság vagy más kifogás miatt jogilag még meg lehet támadni. Ezek közül most, a minisztériumok átvizsgálása során több is elő fog kerülni. Az ügyek egy részében most is zajlik rendőrségi vagy ügyészségi nyomozás. Ezek közül azokban, amelyeket az NVVH elkér, ők folytathatják majd a nyomozást és a nyomozást korábban folytató szervezetnek fel kell hagynia azzal. Mi alapján indítanak el egy-egy nyomozást? Unger szerint több lehetőség van erre, a legegyszerűbb az, hogy kapnak egy bejelentést. Kidolgoznak ezen kívül egy úgynevezett „közvagyonvédelmi kockázati módszertant”, amely egy sztenderdizált módszertan lesz arra, hogy kiszúrják azokat a gyanús ügyeket, ahol aztán maguktól elkezdhetnek nyomozni. Az RTL rákérdezett arra, hogy a hivatal mennyire lesz politikailag befolyásolható, a kormány adhat-e majd például utasításokat nekik. Unger erre azt mondta, hogy egyértelműen nem. „Engem ne hívogasson se Magyar Péter, se senki más” – fogalmazott, hozzátéve, hogy ha Magyar Péter felhívná, akkor azt mondaná neki, hogy tegyen állampolgári bejelentést a hivatalnál, és azt az összes többi bejelentéshez hasonlóan kivizsgálják. Az RTL rákérdezett arra, hogy Magyar Péter egy pénteki posztjában azt írta, hogy „Tasnády Katalin lesz valószínűleg a hivatal legfontosabb vezetője”. Ez azért érdekes megfogalmazás, mert Tasnády elnökhelyettes, és a főnöke hivatalosan az elnök, vagyis Unger. Unger az RTL-nek azt mondta, hogy bizonyos értelemben szerinte is Tasnády munkája a legfontosabb, mert ő felel azért, hogy minél több ügyet le tudjanak nyomozni, a nyomozás minél hatékonyabban menjen. „A hivatal elnöke nem egy Sherlock Holmes-ba öltött Robin Hood, aki kinyomozza és aztán elkobozza a (vagyonokat)” – mondta. Az elnöknek elmondása szerint az a feladata, hogy megszervezze a négy alelnök alá tartozó szakmai stábokat, amikkel ők aztán zavartalanul végezhetik a munkájukat. Az elnök feladata, hogy megvédje a szervezetet a külső támadásoktól, attól, hogy külső hatás alatt kelljen dolgozniuk. A Telex Facebook-oldalán megjelent cikk egyik első kommentelője Magyar Péter miniszterelnök volt, aki a címre – Engem ne hívogasson se Magyar Péter, se senki más! – reagálva ezt írta: Mondjuk nem is terveztem! https://www.politico.eu/article/governme.text: PARIS — The French government failed Monday to convince students to end their protests. On the sidelines of meetings with Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu and education and university ministers Édouard Geffray and Philippe Baptiste, representatives of high school and university students made it clear they were not yet satisfied with the government’s proposals and vowed to keep protesting. “Not all our demands have been satisfied, and we will see this through to the end,” Louis Letoublon, vice-president of the organization “Les Lycéens!” said after the meeting, calling on high school students to continue protests on Oct. 31 and Nov. 5. Advertisement Advertisement Students have demanded up to 250,000 extra places in higher education and universities, better conditions in educational institutions, more teachers and a major overhaul of the selection process for university entry. On Monday, the government told students it would look into reforming France’s university admissions platform, Parcoursup, which student groups consider opaque and a source of inequality, starting in 2028. It also promised more money to renovate schools, an extra 15,000 places in higher education in industry, health and technical education, and a maximum of 28 students per classroom in the first year of high school. Those measures, widely reported by French media and confirmed by student representatives who attended the meetings, will be detailed at a press conference later this evening. But university students are not impressed. “Once again, the government is missing the point. If the government’s strategy is to show contempt for our demands, then we will remain mobilized in the streets and on university campuses, and we won’t back down,” university union UNEF said earlier in the afternoon, when news of the government’s proposals began to circulate. Student demonstrations and blockades in schools and universities earlier this month were among the first expressions of broader social unrest, which later turned into protests over the cost of living and spiraled into riots two weeks ago. https://www.pokernews.com/news/2026/10/r.text: Tap the button in Safari Select “Add to Home Screen” Tap “Add” Hungary's Richard Broda Captures 888LIVE London Mini Main Title Matthew Pitt Senior Editor Add as preferred on Google Copy link Share on Twitter Share on Facebook Oct 15, 2026 2 min read Table Of Contents £340 Mini Main Final Table Results Follow all the £2,000 High Roller Action The decision to travel from Hungary to the United Kingdom has proved to be a profitable one for Richard Broda after he became the £340 Mini Main champion at the 888LIVE London festival. Broda was one of 402 entrants who helped create a £114,560 prize pool . After sitting down at the nine-handed final table third in chips, Broda eventually emerged victorious and with a £26,220 prize. That sum represents the Hungarian's third-largest score, bested only by the $55,000 he collected from the 2025 World Series of Poker (WSOP) Paradise Super Main Event , and his massive $307,000 haul from a runner-up finish in the 2025 Dolce Vita Series in Northern Cyprus. Several household names reached the top 50 and received a payout. They included Oliver Hutchins , Christopher Day , Adam Wilkinson , Vikram Mehta , and Yucel Eminoglu . £340 Mini Main Final Table Results Rank Player Prize 1 Richard Broda £26,220 2 Guang Yang £17,520 3 Pranav Agarwal £11,490 4 Michael Long £7,580 5 Tomas Dailidonis £5,170 6 Philip Corion £3,730 7 Greg Hawes £2,860 8 Hanyang Shi £2,300 9 Artin Bazai £1,900 Artin Bazai sat down at the final table with by far the shortest stack, and he couldn't rectify his lowly position. Bazai busted in ninth for a £1,900 score, giving the remaining players a little more elbow room. Eighth place and £2,300 went to Hanyang Shi before Greg Hawes was eliminated in seventh for £2,860. The final table lost Philip Corion in sixth place, a finish good for £3,730. Corion recently reached the final table of the €1,650 No-Limit Hold'em Mystery Bounty event at the European Poker Tour (EPT) Barcelona festival and walked away with €30,600. Poker Legend John Duthie Victorious at 888LIVE London Read more Lithuanian Tomas Dailidonis, who reached three final tables and won $56,237 in Las Vegas in early September, saw his latest deep run end in a fifth-place finish worth £5,170, with Michael Long collecting a career-best £7,580 when he busted in fourth. The final three players were now guaranteed a five-figure sum for their efforts. India's Pranav Agarwal banked £11,490 when he was eliminated in third. Agarwal has been in solid form for the past 12 months, enjoying results such as a third-place finish in the £1,500 WSOP Circuit Main Event in Nottingham (£88,195), a win in the £550 GUKPT UK Open Cup (£23,411), and a runner-up finish in the £1,250 GUKPT Luton Main Event (£39,310). Heads-up saw Broda go head-to-head with Guang Yang, the latter making his third final table appearance of his fledgling career. Broda's superior experience shone through, and he defeated Yang to claim the title, the trophy, and £26,220, which edges his recorded live tournament winnings closer to $500,000. Yang netted £17,520, beating his previous best score by more than twice. Only 18 of the 64 entrants remain in the hunt for the title, though that number is set to increase as late registration remains open until the start of play. Among those who advanced from Day 1 include National Poker League (NPL) leader Bryan Taylor , Andrew Hulme , John Duthie , Joe Hindry , Brandon Sheils , Youness Barakat , Arthur Conan , and 888 ambassador Lucia Navarro . https://www.israelnationalnews.com/news/.text: The year was 1536 from Creation (2584 B.C.E.), Noach was 480 years old, humanity was in its tenth generation, and “Hashem saw that Man’s evil on the earth was great, and all he thought about was evil all day; so Hashem regretted having made Man in the world, even though this saddened Him" (Genesis 6:5-6). Despite His sadness, G-d decreed that the world would be destroyed by a flood. Only Noach and his immediate family would survive, to repopulate the earth. Why Noach? Because “Noach found favour in Hashem’s eyes" (v. 8). With these words we concluded Parashat Bereishit last week. I note, briefly and as an aside, that these final words in Parashat Bereishit already allude to how Noach would save humanity from complete annihilation 120 years hence: וְנֹחַ מָצָא חֵן בְּעֵינֵי ה' “Noach found favour in Hashem’s eyes". The final four words are מָצָא חֵן בְּעֵינֵי ה', and the final letters of these four words are אֳנִיָּה, meaning “boat" - an allusion to the Ark. What sealed humanity’s fate of destruction was that “the earth was corrupted before G-d, and the earth was filled with hamas " (v.11). There are different opinions of what the Hebrew word חָמָס, hamas , means: According to Rashi and Mizrachi it denotes robbery - not ordinary theft, which might be done in secret, but specifically brazen and violent robbery committed openly. According to the Ibn Ezra it denotes a combination of violent robbery, oppression, exploitation, and violent rape of women. According to the Ohr ha-Chayim it is an all-encompassing term for general evil, including violent robbery, sexual immorality, murder, and idolatry. According to Rabbi Shimshon Raphael Hirsch it denotes injustices which individually are too petty and minor to be brought before human courts, and which are therefore impossible for the victims to be compensated for, but which cumulatively destroy human society. G-d introduced His reason for the impending destruction with the words: לֹא־יָדוֹן רוּחִי בָֽאָדָם לְעֹלָם, בְּשַׁגַּם הוּא בָשָׂר; וְהָיוּ יָמָיו מֵאָה וְעֶשְׂרִים שָׁנָֽה: “My spirit will not abide in Man forever, since he is no more than mortal flesh; and his days will be a hundred and twenty years" (Genesis 6:3). However this translation (which is the standard translation) is inadequate. The Hebrew word יָדוֹן, which is usually translated “abide", really connotes “judge"; hence “My spirit will not judge Man forever, since he is no more than mortal flesh" might be a better rendering. Or more freely and idiomatically, “My spirit will not judge Man too harshly, since he is no more than mortal flesh". The Midrash offers several insights: Rabbi Yishmael son of Rabbi Yossi, a fifth-generation (late 2nd century) Tanna, interpreted it to mean: “I will not put My spirit into them when I will give the righteous their reward in the future time to come" (Bereishit Rabbah 26:6). This refers to the statement in the Mishnah that “the generation of the Flood have no share in the World to Come" (Sanhedrin 10:3). According to Rabbi Yishmael, the generation of the Flood were so irretrievably evil that they were wiped out in this world, and not one of them will be resurrected in the future time to come. A generation before Rabbi Yishmael, the Tanna Rabbi Elazar son of Shammu’a offered another, maybe starker, insight: “Wherever there is no judgment, there is judgement" (Bereishit Rabbah 26:6); the Mattanot Kehunah (commentary to the Midrash written by Rabbi Yissachar Berman ben Naftali, Poland, 16th century) explains: “Wherever there is no judgment in this lower world, there is judgement in the Upper World". If humans don’t enforce justice on human society, then G-d will enforce His justice. And confirming this, the Midrash continues by citing the otherwise unknown Rav Bibi son of Rabbi Ami, who followed Rabbi Elazar’s interpretation: “If they do not judge, then My Spirit will judge them" (again following the Mattanot Kehunah). And then the Midrash cites the greatest of them all, Rabbi Akiva, who applied to the generation of the Flood the verse from the Psalms, “Why does the evil man blaspheme against G-d, saying in his heart, You will not judge?" (Psalms 10:13). The generation of the Flood, said Rabbi Akiva, proclaimed that לֵית דִּין וְלֵית דַּיָּן, “there is no justice and there is no judge". But, he continued, אִית דִּין וְאִית דַּיָּן, “there is justice and there is a Judge". It is striking that that first person who ever claimed that לֵית דִּין וְלֵית דַּיָּן, “there is no justice and there is no judge" was Cain: The Torah tells us very tersely that “Cain spoke to Abel his brother; and when they were in the field, Cain arose over Abel his brother and killed him" (Genesis 4:8). The Targum Yonatan reveals more of the episode: “Cain said to his brother Abel, ‘Come, let’s both of us go out into the field’. When they had both gone out into the field, Cain spoke and said to Abel: ‘I observe that the world was created through mercy, but that it is not governed by the fruits of good deeds, and that there is favouritism in judgment. Why was your offering accepted, while mine was not accepted favourably?!" “Abel answered Cain: ‘The world was indeed created through mercy, and it is indeed governed by the fruits of good deeds, and there is no favouritism in judgment. Because the fruits of my deeds were better than yours and preceded yours, my offering was accepted favourably’. “Cain answered Abel: ‘לֵית דִּין וְלֵית דַּיָּן, there is no judgment and no Judge, no World to Come, no good reward for the righteous, and no punishment of the wicked’. “Abel answered: ‘There is indeed judgment and there is indeed a Judge; there is a World to Come, there is good reward for the righteous, and there is punishment for the wicked’. “They disputed these issues in the field, until Cain rose against his brother Abel, drove a stone into his forehead, and killed him" (Targum Yonatan, Genesis 4:8). Cain becomes the first human being to articulate the denial of divine judgment: לֵית דִּין וְלֵית דַּיָּן, “there is no judgment and no Judge, there is no judgment and no Judge, no World to Come, no good reward for the righteous, and no punishment of the wicked" - and the consequence is the first murder in human history. The generation of the Flood, who similarly believed that לֵית דִּין וְלֵית דַּיָּן, there is no judgment and no Judge, had no restraints on their basest animal instincts, and human society degenerated to such a low level that G-d Himself and no recourse other than global deluge to wipe humanity out and begin again with Noach and his family, the only righteous people who remained. The beginning of the Torah, the very foundation of Judaism, is that G-d created all existence. He created life. He created Man in His own image, inherently knowing good and evil, right and wrong. The Torah teaches us respect for life - all life, human life above all. Without G-d, there is no objective morality, no absolute truth, no justice and no Judge, no reward for the righteous and no punishment for the evil. An almost-contemporary Gedol ha-Dor, Rabbi Meir Kahane Hy"d (USA and Israel, 1932-1991), noted the contrast between “yesterday’s idolatry, which at least accepted the authority of a higher power in spite of its false beliefs", and “today’s…human culture, which in practice denies all higher power, and who have crowned themselves and their own wisdom as sovereign". And, he concludes, “those who deny any and all higher powers are incomparably more dangerous than the idolaters" (Ohr ha-Ra’ayon, page 43, chapter 5, “Accepting the Yoke of Heaven"). Some 800 years ago, the Rambam argued similarly: “No one who worshipped idols ever believed that there was no other god; they never ever imagined, and never will imagine, that the statue that they fashioned from metal or stone or wood was what had created the Heavens and the earth, or that it is this statue that rules them. Rather, even though they worship it, it is merely an intermediary between them and the true G-d… “No Torah-authority disputes this. Those idolaters believed in the reality of the Creator, however much this belief was distorted into heresy…because it is fitting to worship G-d alone… “[And one] who doesn’t believe in His existence at all…or who ascribes some deficiency to Him, is indisputably worse than an outright idolater, for whom the idol is an intermediary or intercessor between him and G-d in his understanding" (Guide for the Perplexed 1:36). The Torah teaches us respect for G-d and for His Creation; above all respect for the life which only G-d can create. History has shown us - and continues to show us, with devastating clarity - that when society denies G-d, any god, even false gods, then hatred and destruction become inevitable. The most famous - well, notorious really - proponent of atheism in modern philosophy was the German philosopher Friedrich Nietzsche (1844-1900), who famously proclaimed that “G-d is dead". And it was a natural progression from that for him to posit that “the weak and ill-constituted must perish; this is the first principle of our love for humanity. And moreover - we must help them to do so" (Der Antichrist, § 2). Such contempt and disdain for life, self-righteously posturing as “love for humanity", is an inevitable consequence of denying G-d. A century ago, on the seventh day of Pesach 5686 (5th April 1926), Rabbi Joseph Hertz (Chief Rabbi of Britain and the British Empire 1913-1946) delivered a sermon in the Bayswater Synagogue: “It was the nineteenth century which discovered that we came from the beast; and ever since that discovery, many of the literary and artistic leaders of the century, and a portion of its directing classes, took it upon themselves to convince us that it was only natural for us to return to the beast. A new and powerful Paganism began its assault against the ancient organised Morality. It dethroned G-d in the sphere of human conduct; derided all moral inhibitions; and declared instinct and inclination to be the truest guides to human happiness. “The twentieth century is continuing the instruction begun in the nineteenth. “A new ethic has arisen, as subversive as it is godless, which bids each man, woman, or child to do that which seems right his or her eyes. It teaches that all moral laws are man-made, and that all can therefore be unmade by man. “There is, in consequence on all sides a questioning of the sacredness of human life, a scoffing at the holiness of purity, and angry repudiation of the idea of property" (quoted in Affirmations of Judaism, London 1927, page 27). It is chilling to see how global human history bore out the brutal truth of Rabbi Hertz’s tocsin within just a few short years. The global catastrophe of Nazism and Communism, two powerful ideologies which denied G-d entirely. When there is no G-d, the inevitable consequence is evil. Societies which believe that there is no judgment and no Judge, no World to Come, no good reward for the righteous, and no punishment of the wicked, can be redeemed only by destruction. Parashat Noach, and all subsequent human history, bears this out with devastating clarity.
